titulo: Hypotheses with «si»: Possible conditions, advice and other uses of «si»

aula.objetivo: Tell apart the three kinds of «si» sentences: a possible condition (si + present), an unlikely or unreal hypothesis about now (si + imperfecto de subjuntivo → conditional) and an impossible hypothesis about the past (si + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo → condicional compuesto), and give advice with «yo en tu lugar».

sessao.titulo: Possible conditions, advice and other uses of «si»

blocos.titulo: Si + present, si no and other uses
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: for a possible condition in the present or future, the «si» part takes the present indicative, and the other part the present, future or imperative — exactly like the English first conditional: «Si llueve, me quedo en casa», «Si llueve, me quedaré en casa» (If it rains, I'll stay home), «Si llueve, quédate en casa». STEP 2: never use the present subjunctive or the future after «si» in a condition: not «si llueva», not «si lloverá». (Exception: when «si» means "whether" in an indirect question: «No sé si lloverá» — I don't know whether it'll rain.) STEP 3: «si no» means "if not": «Si no estudias, no aprobarás». It's two words; «sino» (one word) means "but rather" (lesson 52). STEP 4: for past habits, use the imperfecto de indicativo in both parts: «Si hacía frío, nos quedábamos en casa» (If it was cold, we stayed / used to stay home). Here «si» means "whenever". STEP 5: a shorter, more formal form uses «de» + infinitive instead of the «si» part: «De tener dinero, viajaría» = «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría»; «De haberlo sabido, te habría avisado» (Had I known, I would have told you). You'll find it in writing. STEP 6: «si» also introduces indirect questions ("whether"): «No sé si viene». It never takes the subjunctive there. STEP 7: «por si acaso» and «por si» + indicative express precaution, English "in case": «Llévate el paraguas por si llueve» (Take the umbrella in case it rains). STEP 8: in polite requests, «si pudiera…» softens the request: «Si pudiera ayudarme con esto, se lo agradecería» (If you could help me with this, I'd be grateful). Combine the «si» part with the conditional.
blocos.comparacao: The English first conditional works in Spanish too: "If it rains, I'll stay home" = «Si llueve, me quedaré en casa» — present after «si», never the future. "In case it rains" = «por si llueve». And "whether" is also «si»: «No sé si viene».

exemplos.ru: Si mañana hace sol, iremos a la playa.
exemplos.pt: If it's sunny tomorrow, we'll go to the beach.

exemplos.ru: Si no me llamas, te llamo yo.
exemplos.pt: If you don't call me, I'll call you.

exemplos.ru: Llévate un jersey por si hace frío.
exemplos.pt: Take a coat just in case.

exemplos.ru: Si pudiera pedirle un favor, se lo agradecería mucho.
exemplos.pt: If I could ask you a favour, I'd be very grateful.

erros.motivo: A possible condition takes the present indicative, not the subjunctive.

erros.errado: Si lloverá, me quedaré en casa.
erros.certo: Si llueve, me quedaré en casa.
erros.motivo: The future isn't used after «si» (English "if it rains", not "if it will rain").
In the «si» part, the imperfecto de subjuntivo replaces the conditional (English "if you helped me", not "if you would help me").
«Si no» (if not) is two words; «sino» means "but rather".

blocos.enunciado: Make three possible plans out loud for next week: «Si hace buen tiempo, yo…», «Si no tengo trabajo, yo…». Then give advice to a tired colleague: «Si fuera tú, yo…».
Complete out loud: «Si tuviera tiempo, yo…», «Si viviera en España, yo…», «Si pudiera elegir, yo…».
